problem_statement: This is a Nuxt 4 documentation site for the PicoIntl message-formatting library, built with Nuxt UI: an Overview reference page at /, a Formatting guide at /guide/formatting, and a Pluralization guide at /guide/plurals, all wrapped in a shared app shell (a sticky left column with the PicoIntl wordmark and an Overview/Formatting/Pluralization nav, and a right column that renders the current page). The docs team wants a small, consistent 'On this reference' section quick-nav to sit at the top of every reference page: a labelled row of jump-links to the sections of the page you are reading (the on-page section list every API reference ships), plus an API version switch in the always-present left shell with a live readout that names which reference version the reader is on. Ship the section quick-nav so it (1) appears at the top of the Overview, Formatting AND Pluralization pages alike, (2) lays out its jump-link row responsively so no reference page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone, (3) matches the PicoIntl green/emerald docs styling (light-green panel, green pill borders, a high-contrast active jump-link) rather than an off-palette dark slab or an illegible pale-on-pale card, and (4) keeps the version readout in sync with the switch so a reader who selects the v1 chip sees the readout update to 'Showing: v1 API reference'. Keep the rest of the site — navigation, the color-mode button, the existing reference copy and the Nuxt build — intact with no console or network errors.
required_content: Add a shared 'On this reference' section quick-nav at the top of the reference pages so it renders on the Overview (/), Formatting (/guide/formatting) AND Pluralization (/guide/plurals) pages (a shared component rendered from the app shell, not a per-page copy).
The quick-nav shows an 'On this reference' label and a row of jump-links to the current page's sections, with the first section marked active.
The jump-link row must wrap responsively so no reference page overflows horizontally on a 390px phone (overflow tolerance 24px).

Style the quick-nav in the PicoIntl green/emerald docs language (light-green panel, green pill borders, a high-contrast dark-green active jump-link), not an off-palette dark-slate slab and not an illegible pale-on-pale card whose title overlaps the row.

Add an API version switch in the always-present left shell with a readout, and wire it so that after clicking the v1 chip the readout reads 'Showing: v1 API reference' — it must re-read the live selection, not show a stale captured value.
Preserve the Overview/Formatting/Pluralization navigation, the color-mode button, the existing reference copy and the Nuxt build with no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Implement the section quick-nav as a shared component rendered from the app shell so a single source of truth reaches every reference page; do not paste divergent copies per page or build a detached widget.
The jump-link row must use a fluid, wrapping layout (no fixed-width nowrap track) so it never forces horizontal overflow on tablet or mobile.

The quick-nav must adopt the PicoIntl docs theme (the green #00DC82 / emerald accent, a light-green panel background, green pill borders, an uppercase small-caps label, and a readable high-contrast active jump-link) so it reads as part of the docs, not a foreign dark-slate slab or a pale-on-pale illegible card.
The label must sit above the jump-link row with clear spacing; it must not be pulled onto or overlap the row.

Place the version-switch readout in the always-present left shell, separate from the quick-nav itself, and make it reflect the CURRENT selection after every click by reading the live selected version, so it can never go stale relative to the highlighted chip.
Do not remove or regress the navigation, the color-mode button, the existing reference copy or the Nuxt build.
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial protect the Overview reference page across viewports.
desktop_formatting, mobile_formatting and desktop_plurals protect the existing guide pages and must carry the section quick-nav at the top.
desktop_rail_home and mobile_rail_home scroll the section quick-nav into view and must show the green/emerald rail without horizontal overflow and with a readable active jump-link.
desktop_rail_formatting protects the quick-nav's presence on the Formatting guide page.
version_toggle_home clicks the v1 chip in the version switch; the readout must then read 'Showing: v1 API reference'.

change_completion: The section quick-nav is present at the top of the Overview, Formatting AND Pluralization pages (the shared component reaches all three routes).

After clicking the v1 chip in the version switch on the Overview page, the readout updates to 'Showing: v1 API reference' — the post-interaction terminal state changed from 'Showing: v2 API reference'.
design_consistency: The quick-nav on the rail states matches the reference's green/emerald docs styling under the visual-regression gate (pixel/ssim/block-fidelity), not an off-palette slab or an illegible pale-on-pale card.
The quick-nav adopts the PicoIntl green theme tokens and light-panel idiom so it reads as part of the docs across every page.
responsive: No captured reference page overflows horizontally beyond 24px on a 390px phone; the jump-link row wraps.
desktop_rail_home, mobile_rail_home and desktop_rail_formatting keep the section quick-nav readable across viewports without clipping or overflow.
regression: Navigation (Overview/Formatting/Pluralization) and the color-mode button remain present and functional.
The existing reference copy and the Nuxt build are not removed or broken, with no console or network errors.

metadata.design_goal: add a shared, on-brand 'On this reference' section quick-nav across every reference page with an API version switch readout, while keeping navigation and the Nuxt build stable
metadata.source_repo_kind: Nuxt 4 documentation site built with Nuxt UI, with a shared sticky app shell (wordmark + Overview/Formatting/Pluralization nav + color-mode button), an Overview reference page and two guide pages, using the green Tailwind theme and self-hosted fonts

design_goal: add a shared, on-brand 'On this reference' section quick-nav across every reference page with an API version switch readout, while keeping navigation and the Nuxt build stable
author_notes: slot_201 DEDUP + L4 hardening onto the nuxt-ui-templates starter Nuxt UI template (reassigned off the shared themefisher godocs-bulma docs repo). The starter is reworked into an offline-clean PicoIntl reference site; the shared docs shell, PicoIntl wordmark, navigation and color-mode button are shared byte-identically across legs. The L4 levers ride on a new shared 'On this reference' section quick-nav component (a native docs table-of-contents feature) rendered from the app shell plus an API version switch readout host in the always-present left shell. reference = quick-nav on all reference pages, fluid wrap, green/emerald light-panel styling with a readable active jump-link, and a version readout that re-reads the live selection (passes D2/D3/D4/D6). baseline = the original unrepaired quick-nav: present on the Overview page only (fails D2 cross-page on the guide pages), fixed 780px nowrap jump-links (fails D6 mobile overflow), an off-brand dark-slate slab (fails D3), but its version readout IS synced on click (passes D4). bad = a 'smart wrong' quick-nav: present on the Overview only (fails D2 on the guide pages), 560px min-width nowrap + a shallow inner overflow-x:hidden non-fix (fails D6), a genuinely broken card whose pale-mint active label sits on a near-identical pale-mint fill (illegible) and whose title is pulled down by a negative margin so it overlaps the jump-link row (fails D3), and a version readout wired from a value snapshotted once at setup so it stays 'v2' after selecting v1 (fails D4) — bad fails 4 orthogonal gates. The Nuxt generate build renders every page with self-hosted fonts and no network calls.
